docs/user-guide/dataex/.title: DataEx
docs/user-guide/dataex/.body:
DataEx › Harness

DataEx is one rail row since 2026-11-21: the Harness (?tab=harness). It is the trust
posture over the data and the platform: what TIDDE found, what it can do about each finding, and who
may do what.
The page



Part
What it shows




Findings
the harness and compliance findings, by severity, each with its Proposed remedy and the actions TIDDE can really take. See Harness findings.


Access
the console's write lists: whether each is set, its size, and whether you are on it. See Access and roles.


Relationship-based access
the status of the console's relationship-based access checks



Acting on a finding
Each finding offers only actions TIDDE can take: dispatch an agent, file a tracking issue, or
acknowledge (it needs a human). Every action asks Confirm: {action}. An action TIDDE cannot
take is shown disabled with Unavailable: {reason}, never hidden, and a page you may only read
says Read-only — {reason}. TIDDE records the intent in the audit chain before it acts; if that
record cannot be written, nothing happens.
The agents moved to AGENTS (Fleet, Autonomy, Judge), the
estate to Intelligence overview, and connections
and runners to Settings › Integrations.

Harness findings: What TIDDE found and what it can do about each finding.
Data governance: The data governance agent's controls, verdicts and what it never reads.
Troubleshooting: Error messages, with cause and fix.

Three rules that hold across DataEx

Reads never dial. No page load contacts a data source. Only an admin's confirmed action on
Intelligence overview (Test, Explore, Access patterns, Map estate) dials a registered source.
Credentials are write-only. No read returns a connection's credentials.
Unread is never empty. When the console cannot read a source it says so, with the reason. It
does not report "none".

docs/user-guide/dataex/trust/.title: Harness findings
docs/user-guide/dataex/trust/.body:
Harness findings

The harness findings on DataEx › Harness (?tab=harness) are what TIDDE found about the platform
and what it can do about each finding.
GET /api/harness joins the platform's self-assessment (/api/measures) and the per-control
compliance findings (/api/compliance) into one list. Each finding offers only actions TIDDE can
really take:



Action
What happens




dispatch_agent
a repository_dispatch to the named agent's workflow, with the console's GitHub App token


file_issue
a tracking issue in the agents repository carrying the evidence


needs_human
an acknowledgement, recorded



An agent that addresses a domain but that the console cannot start is shown as an unavailable
action with the reason, never hidden.
Acting on a finding (POST /api/harness/{id}/act) runs in this order:

a session, and the agent-admin list;
the finding must be live now;
the autonomy level must not be off;
a repeat within the idempotency window replays the earlier result instead of acting twice;
audit before act: if the intent record is not durable in the audit chain, nothing happens
and the answer is 503;
act, then record the outcome.


Note: An act is taken by a signed-in admin, unless Autonomy
has armed unattended execution and the action class is at auto; then the harness acts within the
armed budgets, and records the act the same way.

The open findings, worst first, are also the Needs attention section of the
Overview.

docs/user-guide/dataex/governance-rules/.title: Data governance
docs/user-guide/dataex/governance-rules/.body:
Data governance

The datagov agent assesses the tenant's registered data sources. It is deterministic and calls no model: a model-authored governance score would be a fabrication wearing a number. It holds no credential, dials no source, and reads no row or cell value.
When it runs

daily at 07:11 UTC;
on an @tidde_datagov issue comment;
on a manual run of the agent's workflow;
when a plan step names datagov.

Arm or disarm it on its page in AGENTS › Fleet.
What it reads

The connection snapshot: a copy of the connection table that the console publishes after every write. This covers the governance and risk-compliance axes.
What Resolve's Explore recorded, read from the console with the agent's own app token. It holds structure and counts only: names, declared types, nullability and primary keys, row and null counts with their basis, the source's PII flag and mask, and access counts. This covers the data-quality and PII-exposure axes.

The agent reads it from the console on purpose, rather than from a published copy: a description is the tenant's schema, so it stays sealed at rest in the console.
Verdicts
pass, fail, warn and unable-to-assess. The last one is the point: a control the agent cannot evaluate is never shown as satisfied or omitted, and it always carries the reason.
Controls
The agent groups its controls into four axes. Each control gives one verdict per connection, with
the reason:



Axis
What it covers




governance
whether the connection says who owns it and which environment it belongs to, whether its type is one the connector catalog describes, and whether its credentials are its own and kept out of its ordinary settings


risk-compliance
whether the connection declares where it reaches, keeps credentials out of that address, and protects the transport


data-quality (from Resolve's Explore)
whether what a source declares about its own structure agrees with what was measured, and whether its tables are keyed


pii-exposure (from Resolve's Explore and access patterns)
whether columns that may hold personal data are masked, and how widely such data can be read




Note: What each control looks for is deliberately not published. A published list of the exact keys,
patterns and thresholds a check uses tells a reader precisely what it does not catch. The console
shows every finding, with its reason and the column paths involved, to the people who can act
on it.

A source nobody has explored gets one unable-to-assess per axis, saying "not explored yet — run Explore in Intelligence › Resolve" (the page is now named Estate). To fill the two data axes, Explore the source on Estate.
The personal-data findings are a starting point for review, not a guarantee that every sensitive
column was found.
Where the results land

The console findings store: the agent writes its findings to the console with its app token, and signed-in users read them there. Findings name column paths so an owner can act.
The living GitHub issue, "🗃️ Data governance status". It carries counts only, so the tenant's schema stays on the platform.

Tests hold the value boundary: no finding carries a setting value or a cell value, and what Explore hands the agent carries no values.
Not the same as

compliance: checks Runink TIDDE's own code against its control index.
risk: govulncheck over dependencies.
judge: judges findings submitted by other platforms. Its docket is on the judge's page in AGENTS › Fleet.

docs/user-guide/dataex/troubleshooting/.title: Troubleshooting
docs/user-guide/dataex/troubleshooting/.body:
Troubleshooting

Every message below is quoted from the source named beside it. Placeholders in angle brackets stand for values the console fills in.
Sign-in and permissions
{"error":"unauthorized"} (401)
: There is no valid console session. Sign in again. If nobody can sign in, check the boot log for the next entry.
🛑 CONSOLE SIGN-IN DISABLED — a sign-in method is configured but the session store cannot be mounted …
: The console cannot reach its session store. Tell your installer; sign-in retries on its own.
 is not permitted to change connections on this console (the connection-admin list) (adminRefusal)
: The allowlist is set and does not name you. The same shape appears with the runner-admin list, the agent-admin list ("act on harness findings") and the other lists. Ask an admin to add you. GET /api/access shows which lists are set and whether you are on each.
this console has no sign-in configured, so a connection change would be unattributable — set the Google sign-in client or the break-glass password before storing or removing tenant credentials
: Writes are refused outright on an open console. Configure a sign-in method. Runners have the equivalent message: "…a runner change would be unattributable…".
no verified console identity on this request (adminRefusal)
: The session carries no verified email. Sign out and sign in again.
Connections
the connection registry is not configured on this console, or GET /api/connections answering 503
: The registry did not open at boot. The console log says connection registry unavailable — /api/connections will report it. The usual cause is that the console cannot resolve the key-encryption key: store/connections seals unconditionally and refuses to open without it.
no connection with id  (404)
: A stale id, for example from a cached list. Reload the page.
expected /api/connections/{id} (404)
: The path is nested (a/b). Ids are plain identifiers, because each id names a credential file.
tidde connection register
no console named: pass --console-url or set TIDDE_CONSOLE_URL.
: There is no default console, by design.
console URL "" must be https: this request carries your console session AND the credential bundle this manifest declares
: Use https. Only loopback hosts may be plain http.
no console session: set TIDDE_CONSOLE_SESSION to an existing … cookie value, or set a console user and a console password …
: Export one of these. Neither is read from tidde.yaml.
the console at  has no password sign-in configured (the break-glass password is unset there); use TIDDE_CONSOLE_SESSION with a session cookie instead
: The console only offers Google sign-in. Copy a session cookie instead.
the console at  could not issue a session (its session store is unavailable) …
: This is a server-side fault, and no client setting can work around it. Fix the console's session store.
connection "" has type "", which this console's connection catalog does not describe …
: The type is not in the target console's catalog (GET /api/connection-types). The message lists the described types.
connection "": settings[""] is not a setting the  connector reads, and this console would drop it silently rather than refuse it.
: Use the setting names the catalog reports. The message lists them.
fromEnv is required — it is the NAME of the environment variable the credential is read from
: A credential entry needs fromEnv, and a value: field is a parse error.
BLOCKED in the report
: A declared credential or a ${VAR} is unset or empty. Nothing was written. Export the named variables.
DRIFTED, exit code 1
: The console's record differs from the manifest. It was probably edited in the console. Decide which side is right, then re-run with --adopt-drift if the manifest wins.
Runners
address "" … — enter host:port, where host is an IPv4 address, a [bracketed] IPv6 address or a DNS name
: Remove any scheme (://), userinfo (@) or zone id. Bracket IPv6 addresses, and use a port from 1 to 65535.
a runner named "" is already registered
: Runner names are unique. Pick another.
runner  "" is already enrolled; …
: Add a new runner to replace it.
runner  "" is revoked and can never enrol again — enrol a new runner
: Revocation is permanent. Enrol a new runner with a fresh state directory.
the built-in "console" runner cannot be revoked — it is this console process (§4)
: Runink managed has no lifecycle.
An estate action ends runner_offline with "connected; …"
: The runner is connected. Estate actions run on the Runink managed runner: choose Runink managed (console) for the action.
runner_unknown, runner_revoked, or failed "runner registry unavailable"
: See the refusal table in Data-access runners. None of them falls back to another runner.
Judgements
judgement submission is not configured (no ingest credential), so this endpoint accepts nothing (503)
: No submitting platform has been onboarded yet. Until an admin issues the token, the judge reports unable-to-judge.
bad ingest token (403)
: The submitter's bearer does not match the ingest credential.
the submission ingest token has no authority here: a platform that submits findings does not judge them. … (403)
: A submitter's token was presented at POST /api/judgements. Only Runink TIDDE's judge agent, with the GitHub App token, may post verdicts.
token does not carry the App's rights for org ""
: The agent's bearer is not an installation token or user token of TIDDE's GitHub App for this org.
this console does not know its GitHub org: the TIDDE GitHub App names no installation it can read and the GitHub organisation setting is unset …
: Mount the App key or set the GitHub organisation setting. Every App-token door (/api/judgements, /api/data-governance-*, /api/session-runs) refuses until one of them is present.
Model plane
modelrouter: inference queue full; retry later or modelrouter: no inference slot within ; retry later (503 with Retry-After)
: The plane decodes one request at a time. Wait for the Retry-After. Model-calling agents already wait out a 503 inside their own window.
modelrouter: no  backend configured (503)
: BACKEND_ is unset for an embedding or voxtral request. Those tiers have no general fallback.
A model card shows a tier as unhealthy while it serves
: The verdict requires the tier to run what its card names. Compare the card's pin with the live model in GET /api/models.

docs/user-guide/forge/.title: FORGE
docs/user-guide/forge/.body:
FORGE

FORGE is a section of the Runink TIDDE console, next to Overview, AGENTS, DEVEX, DataEx and Intelligence: the studio inside TIDDE that builds web apps and RIVER pipelines. FORGE and TIDDE are one app, and FORGE is its canvas-style side: FORGE's services run inside the TIDDE console, on the console's own session, and FORGE › Studio is a console route, the lanes canvas. It has no domain, no OAuth client, no sign-in, no namespace and no service of its own. TIDDE also verifies every repository FORGE creates.

Warning: Who may make FORGE write to GitHub. Creating a repository, filing work and approving lane changes are refused unless you are the installation's FORGE owner. When no FORGE owner is set, nobody may, unlike the console's other access lists, where unset means every signed-in operator. FORGE's reads (the studio, the chat history, the planner) need only a TIDDE session.

This section covers FORGE as TIDDE serves and verifies it.

Chats and projects: New chat, the Chats history, the Studio, renaming and deleting a project, deep links.
Project manifest & pipeline files: forge.yaml spec v1 and what TIDDE checks in .dsl / .herd files.
Central verification (core/ci): How TIDDE finds, verifies and reports on every forged commit.
Verification profiles: The forge, web and pipeline profiles, and the forgecheck subcommands.
API Reference: The studio capabilities endpoint and link parameters.
Troubleshooting: Capability notices and core/ci descriptions: cause and fix.

How the pieces fit



Piece
Where it lives
What it does




FORGE › Studio
console rail, tab forgeStudio
The lanes canvas as a console route, under a page header that names the chat and its project, with a notice for each missing capability (GET /api/forge-studio)


Chat history
the Studio header's Chats button
FORGE's recent chats, read from FORGE's in-process ChatService; the rail itself has only "New chat"


FORGE services
the TIDDE console
FORGE's Identity, Forge, Project and chat services on the console's gRPC-web server; GitHub writes only for the FORGE owner


Central verification
a TIDDE workflow
Verifies every private forged repository and posts the core/ci commit status


Forger
a TIDDE workflow
Takes the oldest open forge-labelled issue and runs tidde session against it. Disarmed by default



GitHub is the database. A forged app is its repository (topic forged). Its work queue is its forge-labelled issues. Its build state is the core/ci commit status on its default-branch head. TIDDE mirrors none of this.

docs/user-guide/forge/getting-started/.title: Chats and projects
docs/user-guide/forge/getting-started/.body:
Chats and projects

FORGE is the last category of the Runink TIDDE console rail. It has exactly one tab, Studio (forgeStudio). Under the FORGE label, the rail has one row, New chat; the Studio's header carries a Chats button that opens FORGE's chat history.
Before you start

Use the web console. The studio is a console route that talks to the console's own gRPC-web endpoint, which only a browser build reaches. Any other build of the console shows "The FORGE studio opens in TIDDE's web console" and does not draw an empty pane.
Sign in to TIDDE. Every FORGE call needs a TIDDE session, even on a console that runs with sign-in disabled. FORGE acts as a named person on GitHub, so it needs a signed-in email. There is no separate FORGE sign-in.
Nothing to deploy. FORGE runs inside the TIDDE console, so there is no FORGE service, namespace or key to wire. What can be missing is a capability: GitHub writes need the FORGE owner setting to name you, repositories need the console's GitHub App credentials, and planning needs the model router. The Studio says which, above the canvas. See Troubleshooting.

One chat = one project
A FORGE chat is a project. A project is one repository, and each component is a lane: a folder that is either a RIVER pipeline or a web app. The lanes are declared in forge.yaml at the repository root.
The rail and the Studio header give you:

New chat. This opens the studio on a new, empty chat (?chat=new).
Chats (the button in the Studio header). It opens a list of the recent chats, newest first, each with a title and an age, plus a Show all control. The row tooltip reads "Project " or "Not created yet", then the lane count when FORGE sent one, then "App made before chats" for a repository FORGE imported as a one-lane chat.

The list is FORGE's data, kept in FORGE's own sealed store. The console reads it with runink.ui.chat.v1.ChatService/ListChats over its own gRPC-web endpoint, on your TIDDE session.
The list has three distinct states, and each draws differently:



State
What you see




Still reading
A loading state


FORGE unreadable
The reason, and a retry


Read, no chats
An empty list. Start with New chat



Open the studio

Choose a chat
Click New chat, or open Chats and click a recent chat. The console hands the studio a new ?chat= value, and the studio opens that chat.

Read the header
Above the canvas, the page header names what FORGE is showing:

For a chat that belongs to a project: the chat title, then "Project  · one repo, a folder per lane".
For a new chat, or one with no project yet: "Nothing is created until you approve it in the console."
While FORGE has not yet reported which chat it opened: "Opening the chat…".

The header follows the chat the canvas says it shows.

Work in FORGE
Everything inside the canvas is FORGE. It carries no menu of its own: FORGE's options live in TIDDE's rail. TIDDE's code states that nothing is created until you approve it in FORGE's console. How FORGE proposes and applies steps is FORGE's own behaviour and is not described here.


Rename or delete a project
Both are in the project's ⋮ menu.

Rename the project changes the display name in TIDDE only. Once the repository exists it
keeps its name, so clones, links and the core/ci statuses keep working; the dialog says so.
Before the repository exists, naming the project still sets the repository name. Titles are
capped at 120 characters.
Delete application (also offered from the recent chats in Chats) first shows what would
go, then asks you to type the application's name exactly. A draft has no repository, so deleting
it touches no repository. An approved project's repository is deleted only when
the FORGE owner setting names you and the repository is provably FORGE's own. Only a session admin
may delete another person's application. Each step is written to the audit chain and shown live.

Deep links
You can link straight to a chat:
/?tab=forgeStudio&chat=
/?tab=forgeStudio&chat=new

A chat id must match FORGE's shape, c- followed by 16 hex digits or repo-. Anything else is dropped. The old tab names forgeApps and forgePipelines are retired, and both redirect to forgeStudio.
The studio link itself takes more parameters: ?chat=, ?panel=, the legacy ?app= and ?cmd=. They are listed in the API Reference.
What happens after a brief is filed
FORGE files a brief as a forge-labelled issue in the forged repository. TIDDE consumes that queue with the forger:

It runs on the schedule 51 3,7,11,23 * * * (four times a day, outside US Eastern business hours) or by workflow_dispatch. It takes the oldest open forge issue in the org, relabels it forge:running, and runs tidde session start --repo  --issue  against it.
If a PR comes out, the issue gets forge:done and a comment linking the draft PR. If not, it gets forge:failed and a comment saying why. A failed issue is not retried automatically: re-add the forge label to requeue it.
The session verifies at the build tier. It rises to test only when the sandbox is available on the runner, and the comment says which tier ran.
The forger never merges, deploys or touches main, and handles one issue per run.


Warning: The forger is disarmed by default. The console roster lists it with Enabled: false. To arm it, set the forger's arming switch (a CI variable), or use the forger's control among the console's agent controls. A disarmed run reads nothing and writes nothing, and its step summary says "Forger is DISARMED". See Agent fleet.

Every push to a forged repository is then verified centrally. See Central verification.

docs/user-guide/forge/pipeline-syntax/.title: forge.yaml & pipeline files
docs/user-guide/forge/pipeline-syntax/.body:
Project manifest (forge.yaml) & pipeline files

FORGE writes a project's layout into forge.yaml at the repository root. Runink TIDDE only reads it, to verify each component separately. This page gives the manifest spec exactly as TIDDE's validator enforces it, and describes the narrow check TIDDE applies to RIVER pipeline files.
forge.yaml, spec v1
A FORGE project is one repository with several lanes. Each lane is a component folder. When a forged repository (web or pipeline, never forge itself) carries a forge.yaml, central verification ignores the repository's topic profile and verifies every lane in its own folder. See Central verification.
version: 1
project: social-ops                  # the repo name (informational)
lanes:
  - id: source-mapping               # ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}$, unique
    name: Source mapping             # free text, 
Fields



Field
Rule




version
Must be the integer 1. A missing version is refused with "no version (want version: 1)". A quoted "1" or a 1.5 is refused with "version … is not supported (want 1)"


project
Informational. Not checked


lanes
At least one lane, at most 50


lanes[].id
Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}$, and must be unique. It becomes the status context core/ci/


lanes[].name
Free text, at most 80 characters


lanes[].kind
pipeline or web


lanes[].path
A relative, clean folder inside the repo. Not empty, not absolute, no trailing /, no backslash, NUL or control character, no .. segment, and unchanged by path cleaning (no ./, // or trailing .). Paths must be unique, and no lane may sit inside another lane's folder. "." is allowed only when there is exactly one lane


lanes[].components
Catalog ids. Informational, ignored by the verifier



Unknown keys are ignored, at the top level and per lane, so FORGE can add fields before TIDDE learns about them. Anything else that is wrong makes the whole manifest invalid. Verification then posts core/ci = failure with the description forge.yaml is invalid:  and no per-lane status, because a half-read manifest could report on components FORGE did not mean.
The file itself must be:

a regular file. A symlink is refused as "forge.yaml is a symlink; it must be a regular file";
no larger than 1 MiB;
a single YAML document. A second document is refused as "more than one YAML document".

A two-lane example
This manifest passes forgecheck manifest. It was checked against the validator built from this repository:
version: 1
project: social-ops
lanes:
  - id: source-mapping
    name: Source mapping
    kind: pipeline
    path: pipelines/source-mapping
    components: [source.postgres]
  - id: dashboard
    name: Operations dashboard
    kind: web
    path: apps/dashboard

$ forgecheck manifest -file forge.yaml
lane source-mapping                           pipeline pipelines/source-mapping
lane dashboard                                web      apps/dashboard
forgecheck: forge.yaml is valid, 2 lane(s)

If neither folder exists yet, the manifest is still valid, and both lanes report "Nothing to verify yet". FORGE declares a lane before its agent writes it.
What each lane kind must contain



Kind
Verified when the folder has…
Otherwise




pipeline
.dsl / .herd files (TOML-parsed) and/or Go packages of a module, meaning its own go.mod or the repo's root go.mod above it (go build, go vet, go test ./...)
Nothing to verify yet: no .dsl or .herd file and no Go package in 


web
a go.mod in the folder (go build/vet/test ./...) and/or a package.json in the folder or in its web/ subfolder (npm ci, npm run build, and npm run lint when the package declares a lint script)
Nothing to verify yet: no go.mod or package.json in 



Pipeline files (.dsl, .herd)
RIVER pipeline definitions are TOML files, features/*.dsl and herd/*.herd. TIDDE's check on them is syntax only:

every *.dsl and *.herd file under the tree must parse as TOML 1.0;
the check is syntax only: the meaning of the keys ([metadata], [dag], [[dag.step]], [golden]) and .contract files are outside it;
the scan never enters .git, .github, node_modules, vendor, testdata, or any directory whose name starts with . or _.

This documentation gives no pipeline grammar beyond "valid TOML", because TIDDE does not define one. A file that fails to parse is reported by file with its position:
::error file=bad.dsl::not valid TOML: line 1, column 5: toml: array is incomplete
ok  ok.herd
forgecheck: 2 pipeline file(s), 1 invalid; 0 Go package(s)
::error::1 of 2 pipeline file(s) not valid TOML, first: bad.dsl

An empty pipeline (no .dsl/.herd file and no Go package) is a failure with the description Nothing to verify yet: no .dsl or .herd file and no Go package. It is deliberately not a skip: a skipped check concludes success in GitHub Actions, and FORGE would show a pipeline with nothing in it as green.
See Verification profiles for the exact commands.

docs/user-guide/forge/deployment-guide/.title: Central verification
docs/user-guide/forge/deployment-guide/.body:
Central verification (core/ci)

Every repository FORGE creates is verified centrally, by Runink TIDDE, and the verdict is reported as one commit status, core/ci. This is verification, not a deploy pipeline: a green core/ci means TIDDE's verification passed.
No per-repository CI
Every repository FORGE creates (topic forged) carries no CI of its own and no App credentials. TIDDE verifies it centrally. Do not add a workflow or a key to a forged repository. A repository is covered the moment it is tagged forged.
The flow

The sweep finds unverified commits
A sweep runs every 10 minutes. It lists the org's repositories with /orgs/{org}/repos, not search: the search index lags, and a repository forged a minute ago is exactly the one someone is waiting on. It keeps every repository tagged forged, and skips archived and disabled ones.
For each target it collects the default-branch head first, then each open PR head. It picks the first SHA that has no core/ci status, or whose core/ci status has been pending for more than 90 minutes.

It claims, then dispatches
Before dispatching, it sets core/ci = pending with the description "queued for TIDDE verification". The claim comes first, so the next sweep skips the commit even if this run dies. It then starts verification in TIDDE with {repo, sha, ref, kind}. The GitHub App reports through a commit status, because it needs only statuses: write for that.

TIDDE verifies
The verification run:

validates the target (org/ and a 40-hex SHA);
mints an App token scoped to the target only;
re-derives the profile from the repo itself. The payload's kind is not trusted;
refuses anything that is public, or that is not tagged forged;
sets core/ci to "TIDDE verification running ()";
checks out the SHA with persist-credentials: false, and runs the profile's checks. No step that runs the target's code has a token in its environment.

See Verification profiles.

It closes core/ci
A final step under always() mints a fresh token and posts the verdict. A cancelled or timed-out run therefore still closes its status, as error.


Throughput and safety rules

One verification per sweep. Verifications run one at a time, and the sweep starts none while one is already waiting. That gives at most six verifications an hour.
Default-branch heads first. They are what FORGE shows. A PR head waits behind every unverified default branch.
Public repositories and fork PRs are never dispatched. Verification builds and runs the target's code on a self-hosted runner. Verification also refuses a public repository started by hand: "… is public — its code is never built on a self-hosted runner".
Stale pending recovers itself. A verification times out at 45 minutes and waits behind at most one running verification. A pending status older than 90 minutes therefore has no run behind it and is started again.
It never merges, pushes or comments. It only checks, and posts statuses.

The status contract
FORGE reads this. Do not deviate.



Field
Meaning




context
core/ci, on the verified commit


pending
queued (by the sweep) or running


success
every check of the profile passed


failure
a check failed, including "Nothing to verify yet" for an empty pipeline


error
the infrastructure could not run the checks: token, checkout, a missing toolchain, or a cancelled or timed-out run


target_url
the verification run that decided it


description
at most 140 characters, and says why



Success descriptions per profile:



Profile
core/ci success description




web
go build/vet/test and npm ci/build passed


pipeline
 pipeline file(s) parse as TOML; go build/vet/test passed over  package(s), or …; no Go package



Projects with forge.yaml: one status per lane
When a forged repository carries forge.yaml, the topic profile is not run. forgecheck manifest, then forgecheck lanes, then forgecheck aggregate (under always()) run instead, and post:

core/ci/ per lane, with the same states and meanings as core/ci. A lane with nothing to check is failure with a description starting Nothing to verify yet. Every lane context goes pending ("TIDDE verification running") as soon as the manifest is read.
core/ci, the aggregate, set to "TIDDE verification running (N components, forge.yaml)" while running, and then:




Condition
State
Description




any lane error
error
N/M components could not be verified — : 


any real lane failure
failure
N/M components failed — : 


every lane has nothing to verify
failure
Nothing to verify yet: no component has code yet


otherwise
success
P/M components verified[, E with nothing to verify yet]



A lane with no recorded result (a cancel or timeout) closes as error: "verification did not complete — cancelled or timed out". An invalid manifest posts core/ci = failure with forge.yaml is invalid:  and no per-lane status. Repositories without forge.yaml are verified by their profile.
Who reads core/ci

FORGE, for its "CI build" stage. This is FORGE's own reading of the same fact.
For every CI agent, see CI workflows.

docs/user-guide/forge/builders-reference.title: Verification profiles
docs/user-guide/forge/builders-reference.body:
Verification profiles

Verification chooses one profile per target. It derives the profile from the repository's own topics, never from the request.



Profile
Chosen when




pipeline
a forged repository with topic forge-pipeline


web
a forged repository with topic forge-web, or with no kind topic at all



When a web or pipeline repository carries forge.yaml at its root, its profile is skipped and each lane is verified by its own kind. See Project manifest. A symlinked forge.yaml counts as present, so forgecheck refuses it as invalid and the profile does not quietly run instead.
Toolchains come from the runner image and are never downloaded per run: Go 1.26 from the baked toolcache (setup-go@v5, cache: false) and Node 24 bundled with the runner at $HOME/externals/node24/bin. A missing toolchain is an error, never a green build. The job's timeout is 45 minutes.
web
At the repository root, then in web/:
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./...

cd web
npm ci
npm run build
npm run lint     # only when package.json declares a lint script

A forged web app is expected to have its Go backend module at the root (go.mod) and its frontend in web/ (web/package.json). A missing one is a failure.
pipeline
Verification runs TIDDE's own checker, forgecheck, over the target, then go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... when it counted Go packages.
forgecheck TOML-parses every .dsl/.herd file and counts the Go packages of the root module. Exit code 1 (bad TOML, or nothing to verify) maps to failure. Exit code 2 (it could not run) maps to error.
forgecheck reference
forgecheck is TIDDE-owned, so no forged repository carries a copy. It has a default mode and three sub-modes for forge.yaml.



Invocation
Flags
Does
Exit




forgecheck
-root (default .), -github-output
TOML-parses every .dsl/.herd under the root and counts Go packages when the root has go.mod. Writes toml=, gopkgs=, reason=
0 verified · 1 checks failed · 2 could not run


forgecheck manifest
-file (default forge.yaml), -github-output
Validates the manifest. Writes present=, valid=, reason=, lanes= (JSON), ids= (JSON), has_web=
0 absent or valid · 1 invalid · 2 could not read


forgecheck lanes
-root, -lanes (the JSON from manifest), -results (required)
Verifies each lane in its folder by kind. Rewrites the results file after every lane, so a cut-off run keeps what finished
0 every lane passed or had nothing to verify · 1 a lane failed or errored · 2 could not run


forgecheck aggregate
-lanes, -results, -github-output
Turns the results into core/ci/ statuses plus the aggregate core/ci. Writes state=, description=, statuses=. A missing results file means no lane finished, so every lane is an error
0, or 2 for bad arguments



-lanes is re-validated on every use. The lanes are never trusted just because they were valid once, and they are never re-read from a file that a lane's tests could have rewritten.

Every message below is quoted as FORGE and TIDDE show it.
A notice above the Studio canvas
FORGE runs inside the TIDDE console, so the Studio is always there; there is no "FORGE is not running" state any more. What can be missing is a capability. Intelligence

Intelligence is what TIDDE knows about the data estate it manages. Since 2026-11-20 it is one rail
row, Intelligence overview (?tab=resolve). Every figure comes from TIDDE's own services: a
figure TIDDE cannot compute is drawn as absent, with the reason, never as zero.
A data-audit status bar sits above the tabs, with Open the data audit.



Tab
What it holds

functional lineage, OpEx, BI modelling proposals (Kimball or Data Vault), CRISP-DM and DAMA coverage

Three rules every page follows

Absent is a state, not a zero. A figure that cannot be computed is a Kpi with no value and a non-empty absent_reason. Each response also carries a Provenance: LIVE, DEFAULT, EMPTY (nothing has been uploaded) or UNAVAILABLE (the store could not be read).
Reads never dial. A page load, a timer or a read RPC never contacts a tenant source. Only an admin's confirmed Estate action dials.
Writes are attributable and audited. Every non-read attempt is recorded in the console's audit chain, including refusals. With no sign-in configured, every write is refused.

how their datasets group into data domains;
how the sources are used;
whether what a source declares about itself agrees with what its data shows.

It reuses FACE's estate engine (connect, graph, access).

Warning: Estate is the one place Runink TIDDE dials a tenant source. The only other dialer is the admin-only connectorsync probe, POST /api/connectors/status/refresh, which covers the connectors TIDDE publishes and never touches registry records. The agents (datagov included) and tidde connection register dial nothing.

The service
The page is the shared estate component (runink.ui.estate.v1.EstateService). Its read RPCs are ListSources, GetSourceDescription, GetAccessPatterns, GetEstateMap and GetReconciliation. Its dialing RPCs, TestSource, ExploreSource, ReadAccessPatterns and MapEstate, are admin-write.
Reads never dial
The read RPCs answer from what the last dialing action committed. Nothing dials on a read, a timer or a page load. A test fails the engine if a read calls it.
The page re-reads GetEstateMap every 5 seconds only while a map run is RUNNING and the tab is on screen.
The four dialing actions
Each is admin-write (the Intelligence-admin list). Each is audited with the outcome, including refusals, and each sits behind a confirm dialog on the page that states what it dials and what it keeps.



Action
Audit action
Budget
What it does




TestSource
estate.test
20 s
Checks that the source answers with its credentials


ExploreSource
estate.explore
90 s
Reads the catalogue: datasets, columns, types, declared keys, view dependencies, and profile statistics where the engine has them


ReadAccessPatterns
estate.access
90 s
Reads the source's own access views over a window of window_days 1..90


MapEstate
estate.map
15 min per run, 30 s per source
Builds the estate domain map across sources. It returns at once and runs in the background, one run in flight per console



A second map while one is running is refused: map run … started by … at … is still in flight; one run at a time.
Credentials are opened with the registry's audited Credentials read for one engine call and then dropped. They are never stored, returned on the wire, logged or handed to an agent. Engine errors are scrubbed (resScrub) before they are recorded.
Choosing the runner
Every action first decides the effective runner (resEffectiveRunner) from the request's optional runner field:



runner on the request
Effective runner




absent (empty)
The connection's binding. An empty binding means console


console
Runink managed, explicitly, even for a connection bound to a self-hosted runner


a runner name
That registered runner



A name must be a DNS label or console. Anything else gets runner … is not a runner name (a DNS label, or "console" for the Runink managed runner).
console dials in-process. The runner registry is not even read. Actions run on console; a choice of any other runner is refused. No bundle is opened, the engine is not called, and there is no fallback to another runner. The refusal names the state it found:



State found
Outcome
What the detail says




Not registered
runner_unknown
Add that runner, or choose console


Revoked
runner_revoked
Who revoked it and when


Pending (not enrolled yet)
runner_offline
The runner is not yet set up


Active, not connected
runner_offline
TIDDE has no live connection to its address


Active and connected
runner_offline
"connected; …". This never claims the runner is down


Registry unreadable
failed
"runner registry unavailable". Never runner_unknown



In a map run, the runner routes every source, and a refused source becomes a gap in the map. The effective runner, and whether it came from the action or the binding, is recorded in the audit detail and in ActionRecord.runner. Runners themselves are managed on Settings › Integrations › Runners.
The values boundary
The estate adapter is the boundary where values stop. It copies structure and counts field by field into record types that have no field for a cell, MIN/MAX, a sample row, a principal name or a credential. Tests guard this boundary.



Kept
Never kept




Datasets, columns, types, nullability, declared keys
Sampled values, sample rows


Row counts, NULL counts, DISTINCT counts (with their basis)
MIN / MAX / mean (a customer cell)


Access counts: reads, writes, distinct principals
Principal names


Outcome, time and actor of each action
Credentials



Explore profiling limits. Where the engine supports statistics, Explore computes per-column aggregates over at most 25 datasets (resMaxStatDatasets). Only DISTINCT and NULL counts cross the boundary. Explore also keeps the statistics pass's counted row count.
No confidence number. Domains carry an evidence class (declared, measured or weak) and every edge carries an evidence kind. A GUESS edge is drawn dotted in the warning tone and is never styled like a declared key.
Storage
The documents are kept in the console's own encrypted store:



Document
Contents
Budget




var/lib/estate
Per-source last action, access counts, map runs
512 KiB


var/lib/estate-map
The last committed map
768 KiB


var/lib/estate-desc-
One source's last Explore, with h = sha256(id)[:16]
768 KiB



What Estate records as data lineage
When an Explore, ReadAccessPatterns or MapEstate commits, the console records what it observed as data lineage. This happens in process: there is no HTTP hop and no ingest token. The edges go into the same observed-lineage store the apps publish into, under the publisher tidde-resolve. The app ingest refuses that publisher name from anyone else with a 403.



Edge kind
Between
From




DECLARED_FOREIGN_KEY
dataset → dataset
Explore's declared keys, and the map's declared keys


INFERRED_* placement
dataset → domain
The map, only for domains whose members come from two or more sources


OBSERVED_ACCESS
dataset → principals
Access counts, only where a stated read or write count is above zero


DECLARED_VIEW_DEPENDENCY
base → view
The source's own catalogue: Postgres pg_depend, MySQL VIEW_TABLE_USAGE. The Lineage page draws these as "Declared derivations"



Not recorded: GUESSED_COLUMN_OVERLAP (a guess is not an observation) and catalogue containment.
Each edge carries only qualified names, the kind, counts and provenance. It carries no constraint or column name, no detail text and no admin identity.
Edges are deduplicated source→destination. Each commit replaces its own scope's claims (explore:, access:, map), and claims expire after 30 days. The estate lineage key is capped at 256 edges / 512 KiB, and the weakest edges are dropped first and counted.
Refusals you will see

On a console with no sign-in: this console has no sign-in configured, so dialing a tenant source would be unattributable — set the Google sign-in client or the break-glass password before testing, exploring or mapping sources.
On the page, the first PermissionDenied disables every dial and shows the console's reason. A FailedPrecondition or InvalidArgument is drawn verbatim and gates nothing else.

More in Troubleshooting.

docs/user-guide/intelligence/knowledge-g.title: Knowledge graph
docs/user-guide/intelligence/knowledge-g.body:
Knowledge graph

The Graph tab of Intelligence overview is TIDDE's knowledge graph of
the estate: the sources, datasets, documents, rules, agents and runs TIDDE knows about, and how they
relate.
Status: built. The graph shows only relationships TIDDE has stored from real sources; it never
draws an edge it has not recorded.
What you can do

Search the graph. Results open in tabs: Results, Neighbours (what a node is connected
to), Details (where the node or relationship came from) and Explain (why the answer is what
it is, step by step).
Look up a trace by its id to see an earlier answer's explanation again.
Open in Knowledge graph from the estate section opens the graph on that source.
You see only what you may read; anything hidden from you is shown as a count, never drawn.
Run now starts an ingest straight away (Intelligence admins only). Otherwise the graph is kept
up to date on its own.

Documents reach the graph through knowledge ingest, which is a data source under
Settings › Integrations.

docs/user-guide/intelligence/audits-line.title: Data audit & lineage
docs/user-guide/intelligence/audits-line.body:
Data audit & lineage

Three views answer "what happened" questions:

Data audit assesses the data estate. It is the third tile of the Overview's audit verdict strip, and ?tab=dataAudit opens its full panel.
Lineage shows how data moves. It is the second tab of Intelligence overview (?tab=lineage).
Deploy lineage shows whether a commit shipped. Despite the name, it is about the CD pipeline, not data. It is the Deploy lineage tab of DEVEX › Agent runs (?tab=deployLineage).

Data audit (?tab=dataAudit)
This is the data assessment. The Overview's verdict strip shows three: Platform audit, Model & agent audit and Data audit. These pages are assessments, not the audit log. The log is DevEx › Audit chain.
The verdict
The page opens on one StatusIndicator verdict over checks it reads from existing endpoints:



Check
Read from




Source connection tests
Estate · sources


Estate map
Estate · estate map


Declared vs observed
Estate · reconciliation


Data governance findings
GET /api/data-governance-findings



A check that could not be read goes, with its reason, into a single not-measured list. It is never counted as a pass.
Actions and the runner picker
Estate's Test, Explore, Access patterns and Map estate run on the pages that own them: the Data audit panel says where each one lives and links there. The runner is picked where the action is confirmed:

Intelligence overview. Each Test, Explore, Access patterns and Map estate confirm dialog lists each source's own runner (the default: no runner on the wire), Runink managed (console) and every registered self-hosted runner from /api/runners (a revoked one is shown and cannot be picked).

A connection's default binding is set in the Integrations › Connections wizard, with the same picker.
The choice goes on the request's optional runner field. If a build cannot carry the field, a self-hosted choice is refused client-side with RunnerChoiceNotSent before any call is made. It is never silently dropped. The field has three states:



Field
Means




absent
Use the connection's binding


console
Runink managed


a name
That runner



That is why managed is always sent explicitly as console.
A self-hosted runner that cannot take the audit answers with a runner outcome (runner_unknown, runner_revoked or runner_offline), and nothing runs anywhere. Audits run on the Runink managed runner (console). See Estate.
Lineage (?tab=lineage)
The Lineage page reads GET /api/data-lineage (session-gated, GET only). It combines:

the declared topology from the connection registry;
the observed flows that apps have published.

Observations come from two origins, and the page never mixes them. Every edge and publisher carries origin: "app" or origin: "resolve":

App edges carry movements and rows. The page draws graph links from app edges only.
Resolve edges carry structure. They are listed under "Observed by Runink TIDDE Resolve". The DECLARED_VIEW_DEPENDENCY edges are drawn as Declared derivations.

Resolve makes the structural half observed. The movement half needs an app to publish. With no app publishing, the gap is named in unmeasured[] as app flow lineage. Per-node DQ and consumers are absent.
How apps publish: POST /api/data-lineage/edges
Apps push their lineage. The console never reaches into an app pod. The body is a bounded rollup of the distinct source→destination pairs the app observed, with movement and row counts, plus the publisher's own status: whether capture is durable, and how many records it observed and dropped.



Case
Response




no ingest credential
503: observed lineage ingest is not configured (no ingest credential; …)


Wrong bearer token
403: bad ingest token


app missing
400: app is required


app is tidde-resolve
403. That name is reserved for the console's own Resolve observations


No observations and no edges
400. A publisher with nothing to say must stay silent



The credential is the same agent-health ingest credential the applications already hold; TIDDE issues it.
Deploy lineage (?tab=deployLineage)
GET /api/lineage (session-gated) answers "did my change ship?" from measurements. Per image, it follows six stages: merged → agents saw it → built → landed in the registry → rolled → running.

The delivery workflow records what it rolled, and the console reads it back.
The build leg comes from the image build's registry probe of /v2//tags/list.
Each stage is ok, warn, failed or unmeasured. Unmeasured is used freely: a build leg with no digest record, a commit older than the run store's retention, or a workload whose pods could not be read.

Add ?sha= to ask about one commit. The answer starts from found: false and state unmeasured, and fills in only what it could measure.

Note: Deploy lineage is not data lineage. It tracks container images through CI/CD. The Lineage page above tracks data between sources.

docs/user-guide/intelligence/troubleshoo.title: Troubleshooting
docs/user-guide/intelligence/troubleshoo.body:
Troubleshooting

Each entry below quotes a message exactly as the console returns it, then gives the cause and the fix. The pages draw these messages verbatim, so what you see on screen is the text you can search for here. … marks a value filled in at runtime.
Every write is refused

this console has no sign-in configured, so dialing a tenant source would be unattributable — set the Google sign-in client or the break-glass password before testing, exploring or mapping sources

Cause: the console has no sign-in, so nobody can be attributed. The estate and Ask refusals have the same shape, each naming its own subject.
Fix: configure sign-in (the Google sign-in client or the break-glass password). Reads keep working in the meantime.
PERMISSION_DENIED on a write
Cause: your identity is not in the Intelligence-admin list. That variable is optional. Unset means every identity the console admits; set, it narrows the admins to the list. On the page, the first PermissionDenied disables every write and shows the reason.
Fix: ask an admin to add your email, or have a listed admin perform the action.
UNAUTHENTICATED

unauthorized — the console session is not valid; sign in again

Cause: the session cookie expired or was revoked. Fix: sign in again.
HTTP 403 "cross-origin gRPC-web is not served by the console"
Cause: the request's Origin names another site. gRPC-web is served same-origin only, with no CORS.
Fix: call the console from its own origin.
Estate



Message / outcome
Meaning




runner_unknown — …, which is not registered in TIDDE (Settings › Integrations › Runners), so nothing was dialled, here or anywhere else; …
The binding or choice names no runner. Choose console or add the runner


runner_offline — …: connected; …
The runner is connected. Estate actions run on the Runink managed runner. Choose console


runner_offline — …, which is not yet connected …
Finish setting up the runner, or check that it is reachable


runner_revoked
An admin revoked it. Choose another runner or console


failed — runner registry unavailable: …
The runner registry could not be read. Nothing was dialled


map run … started by … at … is still in flight; one run at a time
Wait for the current map run to finish


no registered source has a connector runtime, so there is nothing to map
No registered source type is supported by the engine


window_days must be 1..90, got …
Access patterns take a window of 1 to 90 days


the connection registry is not open on this console: …
The console's registry did not open. Check the key-encryption key and the store



Plan runs



Message
Meaning




four eyes: … started … and may not decide its approval
The run's initiator cannot approve it


A step ends TIMED_OUT
The agent's step report never arrived. Check the agent's workflow run and its playbook-step-report.sh step



Step-report door: 401 missing bearer token, 404 unknown run "…", 409 step … of … is not awaiting a report … or … awaits a report from agent "…", not "…".
Ask



Status / message
Fix




UNAVAILABLE inference not configured (the model router address unset) — no model was called
Point the console at the model router


UNAVAILABLE the sovereign model could not be reached, so this Ask stopped: …
Check the inference plane (DEVEX › Clusters, serving tiers)


PERMISSION_DENIED (the guardrail's own wording)
The question or the answer was blocked by the console's guardrails


INVALID_ARGUMENT question is … bytes; the limit is 2000
Shorten the question


INVALID_ARGUMENT scope must be INTELLIGENCE or DATAEX
Set the scope


Answer STOPPED with a stop_reason
A step, token or deadline limit was hit. Ask a narrower question



Lineage ingest



Response
Fix




503 observed lineage ingest is not configured (no ingest credential; …)
the ingest credential is not configured on the console


403 bad ingest token
The caller holds a different token



An empty page is not an error
An EMPTY provenance means nothing has been uploaded or explored, and the page says so. An UNAVAILABLE provenance means the store could not be read, and the page gives the store's reason. Neither is drawn as zero..

Problems with signing in, with refused changes, and with reading the Overview. Messages are quoted as

DEVEX, DataEx,

Signing in



Message
What it means

docs/admin-guide/.title: Admin guide
docs/admin-guide/.body:
Admin guide

The Admin guide is for a customer's TIDDE administrators: who may use TIDDE, what it connects to, and
how it is set up. The rail footer holds the rows it covers: Admin (only for an admin of the
instance in focus) and Settings.

Access and roles: Approved accounts, roles, the Admin page, write lists, and the accounts TIDDE provides for each app.
Integrations › Connections: Data sources, knowledge ingest, and registering connections.
Integrations › Runners: The managed runner, adding and deploying a self-hosted runner.
Personas: The role you look at TIDDE as, which are on, and the default.
Trial and subscription: What an admin needs to know about the trial and Billing. Prices are on runink.org.

Settings
Settings is one page with these sections:



Section
What it holds
Who sees it




User
who is signed in and how, the session, the instances you may use, Sign out and Sign out everywhere, appearance, language, legal notices
everyone


Integrations
Connections (?tab=connections) and Runners (?tab=runners); see Integrations and Runners
platform console


Personas
Use this persona; an admin turns personas on or off and sets the default. See Personas
platform console


Briefs
recurring briefs Ask TIDDE prepares for you: Pause, Resume, Delete. A brief is created from the chat, through an approval card
platform console


Chat history
your earlier Ask TIDDE chats, grouped by persona
platform console


Billing
your subscription and invoices; see Trial and subscription
everyone



Platform settings
On Admin › Platform settings (platform console only) an admin sets the GitHub organisation and

Access and roles.

docs/admin-guide/access-and-roles/.title: Access and roles
docs/admin-guide/access-and-roles/.body:
Access and roles

TIDDE admits approved accounts only. Creating an account on the sign-in page does not give access. This page
describes who decides access, the roles, the Admin page, the console's write lists, and how TIDDE
hands each Runink application the accounts and roles it may serve.
Who may sign in

Sign-in is Google only, against a list of approved addresses. An address that is not on the
list is refused, and an empty list refuses everyone:. An installation
can instead admit every verified address of one approved domain.
Admins are added by Runink. Ask Runink to add or remove an admin; it is recorded as a request
and applied by TIDDE, which is the single writer of accounts.
Members are added by an instance admin, on the Admin page (below).
Each installation also has a break-glass administrator sign-in for the installer, described in the
private install guide.

Roles
A member of an instance has one role:



Role
May




admin
everything a writer may, plus manage the instance's members on the Admin page


writer
use the instance and change what the console lets a writer change


reader
read only



A role can carry an expiry date, after which the grant lapses on its own. During a trial every
account has the same 14-day trial; see Trial and subscription.
The Admin page
Admin (?tab=admin) sits at the top of the rail footer. The rail draws it only when the server
says you administer the instance in focus (drilled into from the Overview's bird's-eye), and the
page refuses to read anything for anyone else. Without an instance in focus it says to choose one
first.



Section
What it does




Members
who may use the instance, and with which role


Carrier: WhatsApp, SMS and calls
the contacts an audit may be sent to, and the carrier this instance sends through. Platform console only.


Platform settings
the GitHub organisation and the repositories the agents work in, which agent features are switched on, and the cloud providers. Platform console only. Saving is refused unless the console lists you as an admin of that setting.



A member change carries the version of the instance it was made against, so a raced change is
refused rather than silently undone. It shows PENDING until the application has picked up the
new list. Nobody changes their own access, and the last admin stays.
The console's write lists
Signing in lets you read. A privileged write also needs the console's write list for that kind
of change to name you; every attempt, allowed or refused, is recorded in the audit chain. The
Harness page (DataEx) shows which lists are set, their size, and whether you are on each.



List
Governs
When it is not set




Agent admins
arming agents, acting on harness findings, changing autonomy, correcting what TIDDE knows, requesting a revert of an improvement, the GitHub configuration
every signed-in operator


Connection admins
the connection registry and the cloud providers
every signed-in operator


Instance admins
Ask TIDDE's tools that change something (for example creating a client instance)
every signed-in operator


Intelligence admins
Intelligence writes, including the actions that dial a data source
every signed-in operator


Runner admins
adding and revoking data-access runners
every signed-in operator; deploying a runner is refused to everyone


Session admins
reading the audit trail and ending another person's sessions
nobody


FORGE owner
FORGE's writes to GitHub
nobody



The installer sets the first members of each list (the private install guide names the settings);
the session-admin list is then managed on DEVEX › Agent runs.

Warning: If an installation has no sign-in method configured at all, the console reads but refuses every
privileged write, because nobody could be named in the audit trail.

Accounts for the Runink applications
TIDDE is the single writer of accounts for the Runink applications (FACE, PULSE and LUNA). For each application it gives the list of accounts the application may serve: the address, its role (writer or reader; nobody is made an application admin this way) and its state. Each application maps the role to its own. A list TIDDE could not provide is named on the Overview's Needs attention. Status: built and in use on Runink's own installation.

docs/admin-guide/integrations/.title: Connections
docs/admin-guide/integrations/.body:
Integrations › Connections

A connection is a record in Runink TIDDE's console registry. It says which external system a tenant's data lives in, where it is, and which credential bundle unlocks it. The registry is the store/connections package, opened by the console.

Note: TIDDE's records are TIDDE's own. TIDDE and the apps share the store/connections package, but each holds separate records. Nothing syncs, mirrors or reconciles TIDDE's registry with an app's.

Create a connection in the console
Integrations › Connections (rail footer, ?tab=connections) is the only place to create, edit, test and rotate connections. It is the shared datasources wizard (ConnectionsService).

Pick a source card. Cards map to types in the connector catalog. A card whose type the catalog lacks is shown as unavailable.
Fill the settings the type reads. Enter credentials in their own step. Credentials are write-only: no read ever returns them.
Choose the runner that will reach the source. Runink managed is stored as "" (the console process itself). A self-hosted runner is stored by name. See Data-access runners.
Save, then Test. Test is Resolve's Test, run through the shared estate server on the connection's bound runner. It is the one dialler, and there is no fallback runner.

Every change, Test and Verify goes through the handler's own allowlist: the connection-admin list for connection changes, and the Intelligence-admin list for Test and Verify, because those dial the source. Every attempt is written to the audit chain. See Access and roles.
Resolve's Add credentials and the onboarding wizard's Add source open this same wizard.
Source types
TIDDE offers the source types it has a connector for: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake,
Databricks, Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, Guidewire, MQTT / IoT, RFID,
GPS / telematics and Flipper. Profiling, statistics and access patterns work for the
SQL engines (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, Databricks). Other types in the shared catalogue (for
example SharePoint, BigQuery, Excel and customer object stores) are FACE's and are not offered in
TIDDE. A connection can also carry listeners (set, verify, install, uninstall).
Knowledge ingest
Documents are a data source too. From a document or file connection, Ingest documents uploads
files from your computer or takes them From a connection. TIDDE indexes them for Search
documents, Grep and reading, and adds them to the
knowledge graph. Ingest is a
connection-admin action.
The JSON registry API
These routes stay available for one release as deprecated aliases. tidde connection register still posts to them.



Route
Method
Auth




/api/connection-types
GET
session. The connector catalog: the settings and credential keys each type reads


/api/connections
GET
session. Lists records. Answers 503, with the full report in the body, when the registry is unreadable


/api/connections
POST
admin-write, the connection-admin list


/api/connections/{id}
GET
session. 404 no connection with id  when absent


/api/connections/{id}
PUT, DELETE
admin-write, the connection-admin list



The write body (connectionWrite) is id, name, type, environment, runner, config, properties, credentialRef and credentials. On an update, omitting credentials leaves the stored bundle untouched. The body is capped at 256 KiB. A nested id such as a/b is refused rather than truncated, because the id names a file in the credential store.
The type is canonicalised on write, so Service Now, service-now and servicenow all store as one type. An unrecognised type is stored as-is, because the catalog is a known-types table, not a closed set.
Register connections from a manifest
tidde connection register  applies a committed manifest through the console's own /api/connections:
export TIDDE_CONSOLE_URL=https://
export TIDDE_CONSOLE_SESSION=          # or a console user + a console password
export MY_POSTGRES_HOST=… MY_POSTGRES_CREDENTIAL=…   # from your secret store
tidde connection register my-estate.toml --dry-run




Flag
Effect




--dry-run
validate and report what would happen, writing nothing


--adopt-drift
overwrite a console connection whose settings differ from the manifest (off by default: an edited connection is a decision)


--rotate-credentials
replace the credential bundle of a connection that already exists (off by default, because saving REPLACES)



The console URL comes from --console-url or TIDDE_CONSOLE_URL. There is no default. It must be https unless the host is loopback. The session (TIDDE_CONSOLE_SESSION, or a console user + a console password) is read from the environment only, never from tidde.yaml.
Manifest format
A host or an account locator is a fact about one installation's estate, so keep a real manifest in the repository that owns that estate.
A manifest is a TOML file:
apiVersion = "runink.org/partner-connections/v1"
partner = "template"               # groups the file; documentation only
description = "…"

[[connections]]
id = "template-replace-this-id"    # plain identifier: names a credential file
name = "TEMPLATE — replace this"
type = "postgres"                  # must be in the TARGET console's catalog
environment = "replace-me"

[connections.settings]
host = "${TEMPLATE_POSTGRES_HOST}"
port = 5432                        # never a ${VAR}: numeric settings are refused as strings
database = "${TEMPLATE_POSTGRES_DATABASE}"
username = "${TEMPLATE_POSTGRES_USERNAME}"
ssl_mode = "require"

[connections.properties]
owner = "${TEMPLATE_POSTGRES_OWNER}"

[[connections.credentials]]
key = "username"
fromEnv = "TEMPLATE_POSTGRES_USERNAME"

[[connections.credentials]]
key = "password"
fromEnv = "TEMPLATE_POSTGRES_CREDENTIAL"


${NAME} resolves inside settings and properties only, from the environment, at apply time. An unresolved reference blocks the connection, which is why applying the template unedited writes nothing.
A credential entry has exactly key and fromEnv. Unknown keys are refused when the TOML is decoded, so a value line is a parse error naming its key path, line and column.
Declare an ownership property, such as owner or steward, so the data governance agent can name who owns the source.
Prefer an ssl_mode of require, verify-ca or verify-full: prefer and allow can fall back to plaintext.

Keeping secrets out of the manifest
The CLI screens every manifest client-side before it writes:

Structural. Unknown fields are parse errors, and a settings key must be a setting that the console's catalog says the connector reads.
Credential screening. Keys and values are screened for credentials that belong in the credential bundle instead, before and after ${VAR} expansion. What the screen looks for is deliberately not published: a published list tells a reader exactly what it does not catch.
Names, not values. The bundle is assembled from environment variable names at apply time. No error message echoes a value.

Every write is read back and compared.
The report



State
Meaning




CREATED
nothing was there. The record is written, with its bundle if one was declared


UNCHANGED
the same connection exists. It is not rewritten


DRIFTED
a different connection exists. The differing fields are printed, nothing is written, and the exit code is 1. --adopt-drift overwrites


ADOPTED
a drifted connection was overwritten because --adopt-drift was given


BLOCKED
a declared credential or ${VAR} is unset. Nothing is written, and the missing variable names are printed



Drift is decided before rotation. The console's PUT writes the record and the bundle in one call, so rotating a drifted connection would adopt the drift.
Two columns are deliberately not answers:

NOT CHECKED: registration establishes nothing about reachability, and there is no --verify and must not be one. The CLI never dials. TIDDE's only connector runtime is the console's Resolve, on an admin's action, so use Resolve's Test.
NOT REPORTED: whether a bundle is present. Answering that writes a GET_CREDENTIALS audit record per connection.

Connectors TIDDE publishes (not registry records)
The platform's own connectors are configured under POST /api/providers (connectors[]) and published to the connectors. They are not registry records, so Resolve cannot test them. GET /api/connectors/status never dials: it returns the last cached probe, and a connector that was never probed is NOT MEASURED. Only POST /api/connectors/status/refresh dials, and it is admin-write under the connection-admin list. The types with a probe are databricks, snowflake, mqtt, rfid, sensorgateway, gps, and the REST systems oms, tms, wms, yms, ims and whs. A type with no probe is reported measured:false. POST /api/providers merges by section: an absent or null key keeps what is stored, and "connectors": [] clears it.

docs/admin-guide/runners/.title: Runners
docs/admin-guide/runners/.body:
Integrations › Runners

A data-access runner is the process that reaches a data source on TIDDE's behalf. It is not a
CI runner. The page is Settings › Integrations › Runners (?tab=runners).

Warning: Estate actions run on the Runink managed runner (console). A self-hosted runner can be added
and reports its health, but an action routed to it is answered runner_offline, and nothing runs.
Choose console for the action.

The two kinds



Kind
What it is




Runink managed (console)
the console itself. It is always there and cannot be revoked.


Self-hosted
a tidde-runner process on a host you run, under the name you gave it



Add a self-hosted runner
You need to be on the runner-admin list (when the list is not set, every signed-in operator may).

Add the runner
Choose Add runner and give it a name, its address, and optionally a zone and labels. It starts
PENDING.

Start tidde-runner on its host
Follow the instructions the page shows for the new runner.

Check its state
Once the runner is connected it shows ACTIVE, with its health as the runner reports it.


Operate a runner



Action
What it does




Edit address
changes where TIDDE connects; recorded in the audit chain


Revoke runner
TIDDE stops using it



Choose the runner for an action
Every estate action can name a runner: none (use the connection's own runner, by
default console), console, or a runner's name. The choice is recorded in the audit chain.



Refusal
Meaning




runner_unknown
no runner of that name


runner_revoked
the runner was revoked


runner_offline
the runner is not available for the action



None of them reaches a data source, and none falls back to another runner.
Runners TIDDE deploys
TIDDE can also deploy a runner for you on an on-premise host, on Google Cloud, on Snowflake, or on
Databricks. Choose Deploy and pick the target. Deploying needs the runner-admin list to be set
and to name you. A deployed runner can be redeployed or decommissioned.
What a runner never does
It holds no source configuration and no stored credentials, and schedules nothing.

docs/admin-guide/personas/.title: Personas
docs/admin-guide/personas/.body:
Personas

A persona is the role you look at TIDDE as: the head of platform, the finance owner, the
security and compliance officer, and so on. It decides what the console leads with and who the chat
answers for. It is a lens, never access: choosing a persona does not grant or remove anything you
may do (that is your role on the instance, under Admin). It is also not
the TIDDE puppy, which is the brand persona.
Settings › Personas is on the platform console only. Each persona is a card with a plain
description, what it decides, what it asks of TIDDE, the pages it opens first, the regulations it
answers for, and where it opens.
The seven personas



Persona
Looks at TIDDE to answer
Opens on




Platform and infrastructure lead
Is anything unhealthy, did the last commit ship, which agents and runners stopped reporting
DevEx › Clusters


Data platform lead
What the estate holds, which connections fail a control, where the data comes from
Intelligence overview


Finance owner, Opex
What each initiative consumes
Intelligence › Overview › CFO


Security and compliance officer
Who has access, whether keys or personal data are exposed, whether the audit chain is intact
DataEx › Harness


AI and machine-learning lead
Which models and agents run, how much autonomy they have, what the judge found
AGENTS › Fleet


Executive sponsor
The overall verdict, which dimension is weakest, what waits for a decision
Intelligence › Overview


Analyst
Which findings and exceptions are open, and on which data
Intelligence › Overview › Analyst



The Analyst and CFO views are the bodies of those two personas. A persona with no dashboard of its
own does not get one drawn with figures: the Overview says it has none (not measured here) and
lists the pages where its figures are measured. No figure appears in a persona's description.
A card names the regulations a persona answers for (for example GDPR, PIPEDA, Law 25, CCPA/CPRA,
SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, 27701, 31000 and 42001, the EU AI Act and NIS2) from the platform's
compliance catalog. This says which regulations the persona asks about. It does not say that any
obligation is met or that the platform is certified.
Who changes what

An administrator (a session admin) turns each persona on or off for the organisation and
chooses the default. At least one persona stays on.
Everyone sees the cards read-only and uses Use this persona to choose their own, or
Use the organisation default to clear it. With no choice you get the organisation default;
with neither, the console is the generalist view.
A persona the organisation turns off stops applying to the people who chose it. The card says
so and the default applies.
Every change is recorded in the audit chain.

Until an administrator saves, the page says nobody has configured the personas: every persona is
on and none is the default. If the stored settings cannot be read, the page says so with the
reason; that is not shown as "no personas".
Where a persona shows

Intelligence › Overview has a persona switch under the title. The strip opens on the
persona's own view (the Analyst or CFO view first for those two) and a persona that opens
elsewhere offers a button to go there. Links such as ?tab=cfoDashboard still open the view they
name.
Ask TIDDE has a persona picker above the field, with a Generalist option. It starts on
your persona (else the organisation default, else Generalist). The pick goes with the question,
so the answer is framed for that role and points to its pages, and the suggestions lead with the
persona's own. The FORGE chat does not carry a persona yet.

docs/admin-guide/trial-and-subscription/.body:
Trial and subscription

This page covers what an admin needs to know about the trial and the subscription. Prices and
plans are not in this guide: they are on the
Runink TIDDE product page. TIDDE is sold separately from FACE,
PULSE and LUNA, and FORGE is part of TIDDE.
The trial

A trial lasts 14 days, and every trial is the same.
A trial is subject to approval like any other access: Runink approves the organisation and adds
its first admin before anyone signs in. Creating an account on the sign-in page does not give access.
To continue after the trial, contact Runink. When the trial ends, the workspace becomes read-only,
with no data lost, until a plan is bought.


Note: An expired trial becomes read-only once the update that provides it reaches your installation;
earlier builds still close the pages.

The Billing section of Settings
Settings › Billing shows your subscription and its invoices from the payment provider, when the
installation has one configured. Without one, it says billing is not configured. A value TIDDE does
not measure is shown as not measured, never as zero, and an estimate is never shown as a charge.
Access after the trial
After the 14-day trial the workspace is read-only until a plan is bought. Who may use an instance, and with which role, is set on Access and roles.

The Developer guide is for building on TIDDE: its APIs, its command-line interface, FORGE's MCP tools,
and the contracts the agents use.

Agents in CI: How the review, fix and audit agents run on a Git host.

The services
The console serves JSON routes under /api/* and gRPC-web services on one origin and one session:



Service
Purpose

grounded Ask TIDDE answers

data estate sources, explore, map, and declared-versus-observed reconciliation

the ops doctor's repair preview and approval

registering a data-access runner, and the runner's own service

TIDDE also serves the shared Runink services the console pages use: access, billing, chat, profile,
voice, reasoning, estate, data sources (connections, listeners, runners) and
judgement.
The data model
The tenant API is the ClientInstance resource; its fields are on
Architecture. The console keeps each store
(agent health, schedules, runs, lineage, findings, judgements, plans, connections, subscriptions) as
a table in its own encrypted root, and every write is recorded in a hash-chained audit trail that
GET /api/audit/verify checks.
Building on TIDDE

Script the console with the tidde CLI or the HTTP routes, using a console session.
Register connections from a manifest with tidde connection register; see
Integrations.
Call FORGE's MCP tools over JSON-RPC at POST /api/forge-mcp; see

docs/developer-guide/forge-api/.title: API Reference
docs/developer-guide/forge-api/.body:
API Reference

These are the Runink TIDDE-side contracts with FORGE. FORGE's services (forge.v1) run inside the TIDDE console and are served on the console's own same-origin gRPC-web endpoint, on the console session, like every other console service. There is no separate FORGE service, no forge-system namespace and no proxy in front of it.
/forge/ and every path under it fall through to the console shell like any unknown path, so the only door to FORGE is the console's own, behind the FORGE owner setting gate on GitHub writes.
GET /api/forge-studio: what the studio can do for you
A read, behind a TIDDE session, for platform users only. It returns one entry per capability, each with the setting that decides it and, when it is missing, the console's own sentence:
{
  "githubWrites": {"available": false, "variable": "…", "reason": "…"},
  "githubApp":    {"available": true},
  "planner":      {"available": true}
}




Capability
Missing when
Effect




githubWrites
the FORGE owner setting is unset (nobody may) or does not name you; or the console has no sign-in
FORGE will not create repositories, file work or push forge.yaml for you. The same predicate gates the write RPCs, so the page and the gate cannot disagree


githubApp
The console's GitHub App credentials are not set
FORGE cannot create repositories or read the org's apps


planner
the model router address is unset, or the model router does not answer GET /v1/models
The planner cannot propose a plan



The router check reuses the console's cached model-endpoint probe and never makes a completion. Nothing on this endpoint calls GitHub. FORGE › Studio shows one notice per missing capability above the canvas.
The FORGE studio reads each app's build state from its core/ci commit status. FORGE is the only producer of forge issues.
Studio link parameters
The link the console hands FORGE › Studio, as /forge/?…: the path is only the carrier, the canvas reads the parameters. The contract belongs to FORGE. Values are percent-encoded, spaces as %20, and appear in a fixed order: chat, app, panel, cmd.



Param
Meaning




chat
The chat (= project) to open: a FORGE chat id (c- + 16 hex, or repo-), or new for an empty chat. View state: FORGE keeps it, so a reload shows the same chat


panel
The side panel to open: components, draft or details. View state


app
Legacy, from before chats: an app name (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,99}$), which FORGE opens as the one-lane chat repo-. Kept so old links still work. TIDDE sends chat


cmd
A command FORGE prefills into its console and never sends. FORGE strips it from its address after reading it, and caps it at 8000 UTF-8 bytes



Console deep links: /?tab=forgeStudio&chat= (and the legacy &app=&panel=).
