Transport
The Intelligence services and Ask are served as gRPC-web inside the console process:

Same origin and session. They share the origin of the console and the session cookie of every /api/* call. There is no separate port.
No CORS. A request whose Origin names another site gets HTTP 403 cross-origin gRPC-web is not served by the console.
Session. With sign-in configured, a call without a valid session is UNAUTHENTICATED (unauthorized — the console session is not valid; sign in again).
Message cap. One message may be up to 16 MiB.

docs/faq/.title: FAQ
docs/faq/.body:
FAQ

Questions that cut across the sections. Each answer links to the page with the detail.
General
Is Runink TIDDE the same as Kubernetes?
No. TIDDE runs on k0s and deploys with kustomize, without Helm. It adds its own operators, the
ClientInstance tenant API, the security services, the agent fleet and the console. See
Architecture.
Do the apps depend on TIDDE?
No. FACE, PULSE and LUNA do not import TIDDE; each carries a test that fails if it does. Code more
than one of them runs lives in shared libraries.
How do I get access, and how do I sign in?
Sign-in is for approved accounts only. Creating an account on the sign-in page does not give access: your address must be on the approved list. Runink adds your organisation's admins, and an
instance admin adds members. An approved address signs in with Google at your installation's
console URL. See Sign in and
Access and roles.
Which models does TIDDE use? Does it call a hosted AI service?
It calls no hosted model. Every model is served on Runink's own
inference servers or on your cluster. See
Models and inference.
Does TIDDE send my data anywhere?
TIDDE reads a data source only when an admin runs one of its actions on Intelligence overview (Test,
Explore, Read access patterns, Map estate), or when a runner you connected runs an approved job.
Reads of the console never dial a source. See
Intelligence overview.
Where are prices and plans?
On the Runink TIDDE product page, not in this guide. What an
admin needs to know about the trial is on
Trial and subscription.
Is TIDDE on Android?
Not yet.
AGENTS
Can TIDDE act on its own?
Plans and automatic actions run only inside an armed autonomy policy, with budgets, and with a
stop button. Self-improvement is off until an agent admin turns it on (it has not run yet). See
Autonomy and
Goals, plans and autonomy.
Does TIDDE change its own code or models?
Self-improvement is built, but it has not run yet. When it runs, every action is shown on
AGENTS › Improvements, and an agent admin can request a revert. Developer goals end in a draft pull
request; execution is off by default, and merging stays with a person. See
Improvements.
Why does the judge report "unable to judge"?
Its docket is filled only by an external assessment platform that an admin has given an ingest
credential. Until then the docket is empty and the judge says so rather than guessing.
Unable-to-judge is never shown as agreement. See Judge.
DEVEX
How long does a coding session take?
Budget in decode time. On CPU-only hardware the coder tier decodes a few tokens per second, so a
40-turn session is roughly an hour. See
Coding sessions.
Where did Argo CD go?
It was removed. Delivery is a workflow in Runink's own CI, and DEVEX › Clusters compares what it
delivered with what is running. See Clusters.
Why are reviews slow and one at a time?
The engines decode a bounded number of requests at a time and the model router queues the rest. See
Reviews.
DataEx and Intelligence
Does TIDDE scan my data every day?
The data governance agent runs daily, but it reads no rows and no values. It assesses quality and
personal-data exposure only from the structure and counts that Explore recorded. A source nobody
explored is reported unassessable, with the reason. See
Data governance.
What is the difference between findings and judgements?
A finding is a claim made by an agent or an assessment platform. A judgement is TIDDE's own verdict
on a finding an external platform submitted: concur, dissent, unable to judge, or out of scope.
FORGE
Is FORGE a separate site?
No. FORGE is a section of the TIDDE console under TIDDE's sign-in. There is no FORGE domain and no
FORGE login, and the old standalone FORGE documentation redirects here. See
FORGE.
Can I run an app FORGE built?
Not yet. FORGE builds and verifies a repository; running a forged app is not yet available.
Who runs CI for a forged repository?
TIDDE does, centrally. Forged repositories carry no CI of their own and no App credentials. TIDDE
posts the result as the core/ci commit status. See
Central verification.

privacy/.title: Runink TIDDE — Privacy Policy
privacy/.body:
This policy covers the Runink TIDDE console, on the web and, once Runink publishes it, as the Android
app (application id org.runink.tide; not yet available), and the TIDDE
deployment it connects to. For the rest of the Runink platform, see the
general privacy policy.
TIDDE is a console for a deployment that you or your organisation run. The app
is a window onto that deployment. We do not host a deployment you run, and we
do not receive your data through the app. During a trial, or when you use a
shared instance that Runink runs, your workspace is hosted by Runink, and Runink
holds its data on your behalf.

Who can use TIDDE
TIDDE is not open to the public. An administrator of your organisation's
deployment adds you. The app has no sign-up form.

What TIDDE handles
Your account

Sign-in. You enter the address of your deployment, then your user name
and password. If your deployment offers Google sign-in, you can use that
instead. The app sends only Google's signed identity token to your
deployment, which checks it. We never see your Google password.
Your account record. Your deployment holds your email address and your
role. The app shows your email address.
Your session. Your deployment sets it, and it ends after 12 hours by
default. Signing out ends it.

What you do in TIDDE
The questions you ask, the chat text you type, the commands you run and the
notes you save go to your deployment and are kept there. On the web, you can
also choose a file to import (for example, a spreadsheet). The file goes to
your deployment.
On your device
The console keeps a few interface choices: your language, light or dark theme,
the last instance you chose, and whether the side rail is collapsed. On the
web, these live in your browser's local storage. Clear your browser data, or
the app's data on Android, to remove them.
Microphone
The web console can use the microphone for voice commands, and only when you
press the voice control. The recording goes to your deployment, which turns it
into text. The Android app does not ask for the microphone.

What TIDDE does not collect

No advertising, no analytics and no crash-reporting service in the app.
It contains no Firebase, Crashlytics, Sentry or similar library.
No location, contacts, calendar, messages, photos or device identifiers.
The Android app asks for one permission, internet access.
No backup of app data. Android backup and device transfer are switched
off for the app.


Where your data goes
The app talks to one server: the deployment whose address you entered. It
connects over an encrypted connection to the instance you enter. We do not
receive what you send. The owner of your deployment is
responsible for that data under their own policy, and the
general policy covers what Runink handles for your organisation's
account.
The one outside party the app can contact is Google, for sign-in, and only
when you choose Google sign-in. Google's privacy policy applies to that step.
We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with anyone for advertising.

Deleting your data

On your device: uninstall the app, or clear its storage.
On your deployment: ask your administrator to delete your account or the
data it holds.
Anything Runink can do: write to the contact below.


Children
TIDDE is a business console for administrators. It is not meant for children.

Changes to this policy
We post changes on this page and update the date below.

Your rights and complaints
Runink is published by Technologies Runink Inc., Montréal, Québec, Canada.
You can ask us to show you the personal information we hold about you, to
correct it, to delete it, or to give you a copy. For privacy requests, email contact@runink.org.
We read that mailbox, and we answer within 30 days.
If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the
Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec or to the Office of the
Privacy Commissioner of Canada.
This policy is governed by the laws of Québec and the federal laws of Canada
that apply there.
